title: RA2 bridge turns every destruction into a Belief event, so destroyed-in-fog confirmations reach belief
description: ApplyEntityRemoval emits EntityDestroyed or EntityKilledByUs for any id in `game.unit.destroyed`, `game.building.destroyed` or `game.unit.killed`. It needs no visibility flag or killer, and the contract doc says this on purpose. The fog boundary exists only on the created event. If engine telemetry reports every destruction on the map (for example an enemy MCV deploying, a building sold, or a unit killed out of sight), BeliefModel.ApplyDestroyedEvents sets ConfirmedDestroyed on the matching contact. That contact then drops out of the enemy army estimate. Events for ids the player never saw are also delivered, which reveals hidden deaths and their timing.
failure_scenario: I ran a scratch adapter test (since deleted). Enemy HTNK id 9 is created visible, then `game.unit.destroyed {frame, id:9}` arrives with no visibility information: BeliefSnapshot shows ConfirmedDestroyed = true. Then `game.unit.destroyed {id:12345}` for a never-seen id: the Belief frame carries EntityDestroyed:12345.
suggested_fix: For removals of non-own entities, require the payload's `visible` flag (or a killer equal to self), and drop the event otherwise. Keep a missing flag as a MissingFieldsReport entry. Never emit an event for an id that is not tracked and not own.

title: RA2 bridge keeps enemies seen once as seen-now forever and marks their regions visible
description: Enemy entities are added only on created/placed events. Nothing refreshes them or removes them when they leave vision, and an upsert with visible=false returns without removing the entry. BuildFrame puts every tracked enemy into each frame and adds its creation region to VisibleRegions. So an enemy seen once at creation is reported as currently observed, at its original position, until telemetry reports its destruction. BeliefModel sets its confidence to 1.0 each frame, and regionLastSeen and scouting coverage treat that enemy region as freshly scouted.
failure_scenario: Scratch test: enemy HTNK is created visible at (100,100) at frame 15. 600 s later, with no further telemetry for it, the frame still contains the HTNK and VisibleRegions = {1,2}. The belief contact has confidence 1 and lastSeen 600 s. The features claim live vision of the enemy base and a fresh sighting of a tank that may be long gone.
suggested_fix: Rebuild the visible enemy set from per-frame visibility telemetry, or drop non-own entities after creation unless a visibility update refreshes them. Compute VisibleRegions from own entities' sight, not from enemy positions.

title: Enemy that leaves vision stays in every later frame as currently seen, and its region is reported visible
description: When an enemy upsert says visible=false, ApplyEntityUpsert just returns. It never removes or marks the previously visible EntityState, and contract v1 has no other visibility-loss or position-update path. BuildFrame then puts the stale entity in ObservationFrame.Entities every frame, and adds its region to VisibleRegions (line 200). BeliefModel.UpdateEnemyContacts treats each frame entity as seen this frame (Confidence 1.0, LastSeenAt = now), so confidence never decays. regionLastSeen is also refreshed every frame for a region the player cannot see. Own units have the same problem: position and health are fixed at the created event unless the source re-sends it, so repair and positioning work from spawn-time data.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary test (since deleted). Setup: cadence 15, 2-region map. Input: created{frame 1, owner 1, id 42, (50,50), visible:true}, then created{frame 20, id 42, (52,50), visible:false}, then credits{frame 300}. Result: 19 frames. The last frame (t=300) still has 1 entity (id 42 at 50,50) and VisibleRegions={2}. The bot believes it sees an enemy tank and region 2 at confidence 1.0 some 20 s after losing sight, and would do so for the rest of the match.
suggested_fix: When an upsert for a non-self owner says visible=false, remove the entity from `entities` so that belief memory, not the bridge, holds the last-seen state. Derive VisibleRegions from own-entity positions only (or from a sight field), never from enemy positions. Add a test: visible:true then visible:false, then assert the entity is absent from the next frame.

title: Destroyed/killed events are not fog-gated: enemy deaths in fog reach the bot
description: The contract admits that the source reports invisible enemy entities (the visible:false case). Even so, ApplyEntityRemoval emits EntityDestroyed/EntityKilledByUs for any id, with no visibility requirement. It also fills Owner, TypeId and Position from the last-seen state. BeliefModel.ApplyDestroyedEvents then sets ConfirmedDestroyed=true on the contact, so the bot learns about a death it could not have seen.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary test. Input: created{id 42, owner 1, (50,50), visible:true}, then later game.unit.destroyed{frame 31, id 42} while region 2 is not visible. The frame carries EntityDestroyed ent=42 owner=1 pos=(50,50), and belief marks the contact ConfirmedDestroyed. A human player would only see the unit fade from memory. Destroyed events for never-seen hidden ids are also forwarded, as an EntityDestroyed with a bare id.
suggested_fix: Require `visible` (or the owner being self) on destroyed/killed payloads, as for created, and report it missing when absent. Emit the event only when the entity is self-owned or the payload says visible:true. Add a fog test for destruction in fog.

title: game.unit.killed is mapped to EntityKilledByUs with no killer field, so own losses count as kills
description: No killer field exists in the telemetry contract or in Ra2Normalizer's ra2.unit.killed mapping, yet every game.unit.killed becomes EntityKilledByUs. This violates the no-invented-values rule. FeatureCompiler.HandleEntityKilledByUs adds the unit's cost to cumulativeKillsValue. HandleEntityDestroyed, which counts own losses and emits MinerLost/McvLost/BuildingLost, runs only for EntityDestroyed.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated. Input: own harvester created{owner 0, id 7}, then game.unit.killed{frame 15, id 7}. The frame event is EntityKilledByUs ent=7 owner=0. The bot's own harvester loss raises its kill value, adds nothing to losses, and emits no MinerLost event, so trade efficiency and the loss-driven strategic triggers come out wrong.
suggested_fix: Map killed to EntityKilledByUs only when the payload names a killer owner equal to self (add a `killer` field to the contract, reported missing when absent). Otherwise map it to EntityDestroyed. Never map it to EntityKilledByUs when the victim is owned by self.

title: MatchEnded and other trailing events are never emitted (no flush at match end)
description: Frames are emitted only when a later event's frame number crosses the next cadence boundary. game.lifecycle.ended is by definition the last telemetry, so its MatchEnded event, plus any PlayerDefeated or destroyed events since the last boundary, stays in pendingEvents. There is no Flush/Complete API.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated. With cadence 15: credits{frame 15}, then participant.defeated{frame 20}, then lifecycle.ended{frame 21}. Ingest returns 0 frames for both of the last two events, so the bot never sees PlayerDefeated or MatchEnded.
suggested_fix: Emit a final frame immediately when game.lifecycle.ended is applied, or add a public Complete() that builds a last frame at latestFrame from the pending events.

title: Frames are stamped with an earlier time than the state and events they carry
description: Ingest applies the incoming event first and then emits frames for every boundary up to latestFrame. So the frame for boundary N includes the first event after N, and after a gap all accumulated events and the latest entity state go into the earliest filler frame. The class doc says filler frames carry no new events, but it is the later ones that are empty.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated. With cadence 15, a single created{frame 44} yields two frames. The frame at t=15 carries the entity and an EntityCreated event with Time=44 (29 frames in the future). The frame at t=30 carries no events. Belief memory stamps LastSeenAt=15 for something first seen at 44, and event windows see events later than the frame time.
suggested_fix: Emit pending boundary frames before applying an event whose frame is at or past nextBoundary, so each frame holds only state up to its time. Put the event into the first frame whose time is at or after the event.

title: RA2 bridge fog leak: enemies stay 'visible' forever, and deaths of unseen enemies are passed through
description: ApplyEntityUpsert returns early when an enemy upsert has visible=false, but it never removes the entity that an earlier visible=true upsert added. Every later frame therefore reports that enemy as currently observed at its old cell, and its region is counted in VisibleRegions. ApplyEntityRemoval (line 159) also removes the entity and emits EntityDestroyed for any id, with no visibility check, so an enemy that dies in the fog is reported to the bot. This breaks spec invariant 1 and the class's own 'Fog' guarantee. The existing tests only cover one upsert per entity.
failure_scenario: Verified with a temporary adapter test. (1) An upsert of RHINO e42 at (50,50) with visible=true at frame 1, then the same entity with visible=false at frame 20, then credits at frame 300: the last frame still contains ObservedEntity e42 at (50,50). Belief refreshes its last-seen every frame, so its confidence never decays. (2) An upsert with visible=false, then game.unit.destroyed id=42 at frame 15: the frame carries GameEvent EntityDestroyed e42, which is hidden information.
suggested_fix: When an enemy upsert has visible=false, remove the entity from `entities` (or mark it unseen) and do not emit it. Emit a removal or destroyed event for a non-owned entity only if it is currently in the visible set. Build VisibleRegions from own sight, not from the positions of entities in the dict. Add tests for visible->hidden transitions and for unseen deaths.

title: RA2 bridge invents empty production queues and zero credits/power instead of reporting them missing
description: BuildFrame always passes Queues=[] and uses credits=0 and PowerState(0,0) until the corresponding telemetry arrives. Nothing is added to MissingFields for queues, which contradicts spec deliverable H ('fields the telemetry does not carry are reported as missing, not invented'). OperationalPlanner.HasRoom returns true whenever a queue state is absent, so on retail the planner queues a new building every plan and never places one, because Ready is never observed.
failure_scenario: The RA2 path under current telemetry: every 1 s operational tick emits a ProduceCommand for the next building, with no PlaceBuildingCommand ever issued, and the budget ledger is charged for each one.
suggested_fix: Record queues (and pre-report credits and power) in MissingFields. Make the observation contract express 'unknown queues' so the planner can suppress queue-driven production rather than treating unknown as empty.

title: RA2 bridge cannot update an entity after creation: own units never move, take damage or change owner in frames
description: The v1 contract (Ra2BotTelemetryContract) and Apply() only write EntityState from game.unit.created / game.building.placed. No event type updates position, health or owner. BuildFrame then reports that creation-time snapshot as the current state in every later Belief frame. If the native side re-sends game.unit.created as a state refresh, ApplyEntityUpsert emits another GameEventKind.EntityCreated for an entity that already exists, so the upsert path cannot be reused for updates. MissingFieldsReport does not flag any of this, because the fields are not missing, only stale.
failure_scenario: A temporary adapter test (now deleted) ingested an own MTNK created at (10,10) with health 400/400, then a credits sample at frame 9000 (10 minutes later). The last frame still reports the tank at (10,10) with 400 health. Re-sending game.unit.created for id 7 at (40,40) with 100 health produced a second EntityCreated event. On retail RA2, RepairController, SquadController (focus fire by low health, retreat by health) and HarvesterSafetyController work from frozen positions and full health. Squads are routed from their spawn cell, and a mind-controlled or captured unit stays 'ours'.
suggested_fix: Add an entity-state event, for example game.unit.state or periodic snapshots carrying id, x, y, health and owner (and visible for enemies), to bindery.ra2.bot-observation/v2. Handle it as an update that emits no EntityCreated event and moves the entity to its new owner. Until then, record the entity position/health as 'not tracked' in MissingFieldsReport or in the README honesty notes, not as current values.

title: Every non-self owner is treated as an enemy: allied players and neutral/civilian houses become enemy contacts
description: The assembler gates entities only on owner == self, and the contract carries no alliance, team or neutral field. BeliefModel (lines 122/188) treats every entity with Owner != frame.Self as an enemy contact. In RA2/YR, tech buildings, civilians and map-placed Neutral/Special-house objects, and any teammate in a team skirmish, have owners other than the bot's player.
failure_scenario: In a 2v2, an allied player's army (visible=true, owner=2) passes through the bot's base region. Belief records it as enemy contacts, FeatureCompiler raises base-threat and enemy-army value, and the arbiter's base-threat override fires. The bot then pulls its army home, and SquadController can target the ally's units. In a 1v1, a visible civilian or tech-building owner is counted in enemy composition and threat the same way.
suggested_fix: Add an alliance or hostility field to the contract, for example an 'allied' bool or a participant-to-team map from game.participant.joined. title: Ra2CommandSink.FlushAsync drops a command silently when the transport throws or is cancelled
description: FlushAsync removes the envelope from the buffer before awaiting transport.SendAsync. If SendAsync throws (an IO error or an OperationCanceledException from the token), that envelope is already gone: it is neither re-queued nor reported. The rest of the buffer stays queued and is sent on the next flush, so the command order the bot issued is lost as well.
failure_scenario: Confirmed with a temporary test (now deleted): submit Stop(unit 1) and Stop(unit 2), and use a transport whose first SendAsync throws IOException. FlushAsync throws, BufferedCount is 1, and Stop(unit 1) is lost. A dropped PlaceBuilding or Produce leaves the operational planner believing the order went out.
suggested_fix: Peek the envelope, await SendAsync, then Dequeue only on success. Alternatively, catch the exception, re-insert the envelope at the head and rethrow, so a retry resends it in order.

title: Entity ids and ints are narrowed without a range check, so out-of-range telemetry values alias other entities
description: TryGetEntityId casts any non-negative long to uint unchecked. TryGetInt and TryGetPlayerId cast long to int unchecked. Out-of-range payload values do not count as a contract violation: they wrap to a different valid-looking value and are never recorded as missing or invalid.
failure_scenario: A payload with id = 4294967303 (2^32+7) is stored as EntityId(7). It overwrites or removes a different tracked entity 7, which merges two units in the frame. A health of 3000000000 wraps to a negative health.
suggested_fix: Reject values outside the uint/int range: record them in MissingFieldsReport with an effect such as 'entity_excluded (out_of_range)' and skip the entity or event.
